Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with symptoms consistent with concussion, including
headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. The mechanism of injruy and the force involved are well matched to
the reported symptoms. Over the course of 16 visits, care followed a typical progression: early focus on symptom
monitoring, cognitive and vestibular rest, and gradual reintroduction of activity, with visit frequency tapering as the
patient improved. Examination findings were mixed. Some findings, including vestibular and balance abnormalities,
support the diagnosis of concussion, while other neurological and imaging-related assessments returned normal
results. No prior injury to the same body region is documented in the available history. Billing records reflect single,
appropriate charges for each service with no duplicated or repeated billing. Current status is improving, and the
patient is expected to return to baseline function with continued self-management and follow-up as needed.
